title: Reviewer rules and contributor docs are different documents
context: CONTRIBUTING.md is written for two readers at once: a developer getting started in the repository, and the standards reviewer agent, which the Pre-PR gate hands the file's rules verbatim because an independent context knows only what its brief carries. The file holds 22 rules, of which only four are actually enforced by a tool today. Once commit-guardrails moves the mechanical ones into configuration, what remains splits cleanly by reader: judgement rules a reviewer applies, and orientation a developer needs. The code-review and retro playbooks this repository uses look for CODING_STANDARDS.md in the repository root by name, and they are vendor-managed and not editable.
decision: Add root CODING_STANDARDS.md holding only the judgement rules a reviewer applies — comment necessity and density, which layer a test belongs in, commit bodies explaining why, the bilingual pull-request summary — written the way the writing-for-agents playbook says to write for an agent reader. Reduce CONTRIBUTING.md to how to work in this repository: branches, worktrees, the commands to run, when a Changeset is needed, and pointers to WORKFLOW.md, CODING_STANDARDS.md, the testing strategy and the maintenance policy. Both files stay in the repository root. The Pre-PR standards reviewer's brief cites CODING_STANDARDS.md instead of CONTRIBUTING.md.

alternatives.reason: That directory means adapter, not authority; scripts/check-workflow.js and the guidance files hard-code root paths, and the vendor-managed playbooks look for CODING_STANDARDS.md in the root by name.

alternatives.option: Keep one file and mark the reviewer sections
alternatives.reason: The reviewer brief carries whatever it is given; a marked section inside a file written for a different reader still arrives as a wall of orientation the reviewer has no use for.

consequences: The standards axis of Pre-PR review reads a document written for it, so an unwritten standard is visibly missing rather than buried.
CONTRIBUTING.md lands at roughly 60 to 70 lines.
If CODING_STANDARDS.md later grows too long, the root file stays thin and chapters move to docs/standards/.
revisitTriggers: A reviewer round cites a rule that exists in neither file.
CODING_STANDARDS.md stops fitting in a reviewer brief.
